name: Osaka, Japan 🇯🇵
subtitle: Japan's kitchen — takoyaki, okonomiyaki, and kaiseki
items: Kashiwaya (Senri Chuo, 3-star kaiseki — the northern Osaka grand table)

Kahala (Namba, 3-star kaiseki — intimate counter)
Taian (Minami Senba, Hitoshi Takahata, 2-star)
Ichibunesakai (Kitahama, river-view kaiseki — the historic wooden teahouse setting)
Mizai (Honmachi, 3-star — exceptional seasonality)
Dotonbori corridor (the whole street — takoyaki stands, kani signs, kushikatsu, Glico man)
Aizuya (Dotonbori, since 1933 — the takoyaki grandmother's recipe)
Kani Doraku (Dotonbori, the giant mechanical crab sign + crab courses — an Osaka cultural object)
Hozenji Yokocho (Namba, moss-covered alley — small restaurants, the spirit of Osaka eating)
Tsuruhashi (Osaka's Koreatown — Korean BBQ, the best yakibiku outside Seoul)
Kuromon Ichiba Market (Nipponbashi — the professional kitchen's market, open to everyone, street eating)
Ichiran (Dotonbori, solo ramen cubicle — queue respectfully)
Sennichimae Doguyasuji (cookware street — the chefs' shopping street, knives + bento boxes)
Meian (Namba, udon as philosophy — cold, thick, fresh)
Wagyumafia (Shinsaibashi, Wagyu beef specialists)
Kiji (Umeda Grand Building, okonomiyaki — the office worker standard for 50 years)

Shoukichi (Hozenji, natural wine bar in the alley)
